mutations.note: each break names what it must cause; a run error or crash is never a catch

known_gaps_register.what: hermetic, on the property test stub DOM, a fraction of a second; each gap plants a made-up value or a few (the parts of a name, a name and the id a link prints, or two or three values of one kind) and expects them to reach the output
known_gaps_register.status_rules: XFAIL: every planted value still reaches the output. XPASS: none does (fails the run: promote the entry). PARTIAL: some do (fails the run: split or promote). ERROR: a crash, or a malformed entry (an empty or one-character value, one value inside another, a digits value that overlaps a planted value, digits that are not 2 or more ASCII digits, an onlyIn that is not an output field, an entry that plants nothing).
known_gaps_register.coverage_rule: every output field in which a gap leaks must have a positive control found in it (heading h, button btn, link a, label lbl); each run and the flip check baseline verify this and fail naming the field. Limits, stated in the file header: the rule is per field, not per kind of match (text or digits), and nothing enforces that a planted value is not a string the extractor prints on its own (a reviewer checked every value by hand in round 8)

flip_check.rules: a fix names the entries it targets and its known side effects; the result must equal both, with no control broken (the fixes are crude, one or two small edits each; fix 5 has no newline in its anchors, so an LF or a CRLF checkout of the extractor both match); the check fails when ANY fix is skipped (its original text is gone: reformatted or really changed), or when the baseline is not clean or a field has no positive control
flip_check.limit: proves a fix is noticed, not that it is safe; see crude_fixes_through_other_tests

malformed entries (a contained value, an empty value, an unknown onlyIn): each an ERROR
a reformatted extractor, whole or in part: the flip check fails (a fix was skipped); in the round-6 version only a total skip failed

checker_faults_found_and_fixed: round 6: full-width digits are not \d in JavaScript, so the first run showed one XPASS that was the harness; the output is folded with NFKC and a positive control in full-width digits fails when the fold is removed (the first version claimed two ASCII controls guarded this; removing the fold left both green)

round 7: the positive controls read only headings and labels while gaps leak through buttons and links, so a checker that stopped reading them showed XPASS lines and no warning; positive controls now exist for every field a gap leaks through and the run derives the requirement from the gaps

review: ten rounds of independent reviewers read the test code and the journal entry with this evidence (two reviewers in each of rounds 1 to 4; in round 5 a black-box audit of the extractor and a journal reviewer, whose report was integrated in round 6; in round 6 a fresh code reviewer who tried to refute the gap register; in round 7 another fresh code reviewer of the revised register and another journal reviewer; in round 8 a third of each; in round 9 a fourth of each; in round 10 a fifth of each); their material findings are fixed in the commits on this branch; two clean rounds in a row have not been reached
